topics.name: Finite and non-finite verbs (infinitive, gerund, participle)

options: Would you mind to close the window?
Would you mind closing the window?
Would you mind close the window?
questions.rule: Would you mind is followed by the -ing form: mind closing.

options: The sun began to sink behind the trees.
The sun began to sank behind the trees.
The sun began sink behind the trees.
questions.rule: began is followed by the infinitive: to sink (to + base verb).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Third conditional: would have + past participle (killed).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After the verb give, use the object pronoun: give him the spade.

questions.after: we plan a class picnic next week?
questions.rule: To make a suggestion with we, use Shall we ...?
decide is followed by the infinitive: decided to go.
May I + base verb asks for permission politely.

chat: Can you please pass the salad?
questions.rule: When handing something over, say Here you are.

questions.source: The king said to the hermit, "Please let me take the spade."
options: The king requested the hermit to let him take the spade.
The king requested the hermit to let me take the spade.
The king requested the hermit that let him take the spade.
questions.rule: A request becomes requested + person + to + verb; me becomes him.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After could, use the base verb: lend. The infinitive is to + base verb: to finish.

options: If you had not dressed my wound, I would have died.
If you had not dressed my wound, I would die.
If you would not dressed my wound, I would have died.
questions.rule: Third conditional: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

options: You should to rest for a while.
You should rest for a while.
You should resting for a while.
questions.rule: Modals like should (advice) take the base verb without to: should rest.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a preposition like of, use the gerund: tired of digging.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: must (obligation) is followed by the base verb: must reach.
A reported yes/no question uses whether (or if), never that.
refuse is followed by the infinitive: refused to return.

chat: Do you need help with your homework?
options: Thanks, but I can manages it myself.
Thanks, but I can managing it myself.
Thanks, but I can manage it myself.
questions.rule: After can, use the base verb: can manage.

chat: Did you catch the bus this morning?
options: No. If I had woke up earlier, I would have caught it.
No. If I had woken up earlier, I would have caught it.
No. If I woke up earlier, I would have catch it.
questions.rule: Past regret: If I had woken ..., I would have caught (past participles).

questions.source: The king stayed to dig, so he was not killed.
options: If the king had not stayed to dig, he would have been killed.
If the king did not stay to dig, he would have been killed.
If the king had not stayed to dig, he would be kill.
questions.rule: For a past fact, imagine the opposite: If ... had not stayed, ... would have been killed.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: spend time + gerund: spent days thinking. The infinitive is to + base verb: to find.

options: Forgiving an enemy is not easy.
Forgive an enemy is not easy.
Forgave an enemy is not easy.
questions.rule: An action used as the subject takes the gerund: Forgiving an enemy is not easy.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Had ... not seen = If ... had not seen; the result is would have reached.

questions.before: When he was young, the hermit
questions.rule: Ability in the past (when he was young) uses could.

questions.before: Is it all right if I
questions.rule: Is it all right if I + simple present asks politely: if I use.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence that begins with 'Had'.
questions.rule: Had it rained = If it had rained; the result clause is would have + past participle: would have stayed.

chat: What did the shopkeeper ask you?
options: He asked me what I wanted to buy.
He asked me what did I want to buy.
He asked me what I want to bought.
questions.rule: A reported question uses statement order, no did: asked me what I wanted.

options: Yes, you may borrows it. Here it is.
Yes, you may. Here it is.
Yes, you may borrowing it. Here it is.
questions.rule: Answer a May I question (permission) with Yes, you may.

questions.source: The king said to the hermit, "How can I learn the right time?"
options: The king asked the hermit how could he learn the right time.
The king asked the hermit how I could learn the right time.
The king asked the hermit how he could learn the right time.
questions.rule: said to becomes asked; use statement order; I becomes he; can becomes could.

questions.prompt: Make it a polite request using 'Could'.
options: Could you lend me your dictionary, please?
Could you lent me your dictionary, please?
Could you to lend me your dictionary, please?
questions.rule: Could you + base verb ..., please? No to after could; lend, not lent.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Third conditional: If you had not pitied; would have gone; would have attacked.

options: The hermit told the king that he must rested for a while.
The hermit told the king that he must rest for a while.
The hermit told the king that he must to rest for a while.
questions.rule: Even in reported speech, must is followed by the base verb: must rest.

options: Have dug two beds, the king stopped to rest.
Having dug two beds, the king stopped to rest.
Having dig two beds, the king stopped to rest.
questions.rule: A perfect participle shows the earlier action: Having + past participle (dug).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Polite passive request: Could + subject + be + past participle (delivered).

questions.before: If he had listened, he would have won,
questions.rule: The tag follows the main clause he would have won, so the tag is wouldn't he?
The perfect infinitive to have + past participle shows an action already done.
Reported questions use statement order: where I was going.

chat: Shall I explain the sum again?
options: Yes, please. I didn't understood the second step.
Yes, please. I didn't understand the second step.
Yes, please. I doesn't understand the second step.
questions.rule: Accept an offer with Yes, please. After didn't, use the base verb: understand.

questions.source: You must answer these three questions.
options: These three questions must be answered by you.
These three questions must be answer by you.
These three questions must answered by you.
questions.rule: Passive with a modal: must be + past participle (answered).

questions.source: If you had not dressed my wound, I would have bled to death.
options: Did you not dress my wound, I would have bled to death.
Had you not dressed my wound, I would bled to death.
Had you not dressed my wound, I would have bled to death.
questions.rule: Drop If and put Had first: Had you not dressed ...; the result clause stays the same.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: requested ... to answer; did not reply; would ever get: base verb after to, did and would.

options: Had the king not stayed at the hut, he would have been killed on his way back.
Had the king not stay at the hut, he would have been killed on his way back.
If the king had not stayed at the hut, he would had been killed on his way back.
questions.rule: Had + subject + not + past participle, then would have been + past participle.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: with + noun + past participle describes a state: with his eyes closed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: had better (strong advice) is followed by the base verb: had better rest.

questions.before: The hermit asked the king whether he
questions.rule: After a past reporting verb, have seen moves back to had seen.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence that begins with a participle.
questions.rule: Having + past participle shows the first action; its doer (King Arjun) comes right after the comma.

chat: Is it all right if I use your bike this evening?
options: I'm sorry, but I needs it myself this evening.
I'm sorry, but I need it myself this evening.
I'm sorry, but I am need it myself this evening.
questions.rule: A polite refusal: I'm sorry, but + reason. With I, use need.

chat: You lost by one run. What went wrong?
options: If I had run faster, we would have won the match.
If I would have run faster, we would have won the match.
If I had ran faster, we would have won the match.
questions.rule: The if-clause takes had + past participle (run), never would have.

questions.source: The hermit said to the king, "Do you not see?"
options: The hermit asked the king if did he not see.
The hermit asked the king if he does not see.
The hermit asked the king if he did not see.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: asked if + statement order; do not see moves back to did not see.

questions.prompt: Combine the sentences using a participle.
questions.source: The king saw the wounded man. He felt pity for him.
options: Saw the wounded man, the king felt pity for him.
Seeing the wounded man, the king felt pity for him.
Seen the wounded man, the king felt pity for him.
questions.rule: Replace the first verb with a present participle: Seeing the wounded man, the king ...

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Could you tell; would rather walk (base verb); If I had known (past participle).
